issues.legal_issue: A holder’s death before surplus land is declared does not end or alter the liability to determine surplus land by reference to the holder’s landholding on the appointed day.
material_facts: The landholder held land exceeding the applicable ceiling on the appointed day.
The landholder died before any part of the land was declared surplus.
The heirs inherited the land and contended that each should be treated as an independent tenure holder for ceiling purposes.
issues.conclusion: The surplus land must be determined by reference to the deceased holder’s landholding on the appointed day; the heirs cannot obtain separate ceiling calculations as independent tenure holders merely because the holder died before the declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961, Section 21 governs when title to surplus land vests in the State, but the liability to surrender surplus land relates back to the appointed day. The Court applied Vicobar Shankar v. Mohan Lal, which held that the holder’s death before determination and notification of surplus land does not end that liability or permit heirs to claim separate ceiling calculations.

rule.if: agricultural_land_ceiling_proceeding and holder_exceeded_ceiling_on_reference_day and holder_died_before_surplus_declaration and heirs_claimed_separate_ceiling_status

predicates.agricultural_land_ceiling_proceeding: The proceeding concerns determination of surplus agricultural land under a landholding ceiling.
predicates.holder_exceeded_ceiling_on_reference_day: The holder possessed land exceeding the applicable ceiling on the day used to determine the holding.
predicates.holder_died_before_surplus_declaration: The holder died before any part of the holding was declared surplus.
predicates.heirs_claimed_separate_ceiling_status: The heirs contended that inheritance made each of them an independent holder whose land should be assessed separately.
predicates.surplus_liability_remains_based_on_origi: The surplus liability is determined from the original holder’s landholding on the reference day despite the holder’s death.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns a holder who exceeded the ceiling on the reference day, died before surplus was declared, and whose heirs claim separate ceiling status, the surplus liability remains based on that holder’s reference-day holding.

issues.legal_issue: After rejecting the heirs’ claim to separate ceiling calculations, the matter may be remanded to allow them to raise other available contentions and submit supporting evidence.
material_facts: The heirs’ claim that they should be treated as independent tenure holders was rejected.
The extent of surplus land still had to be determined by reference to the deceased holder’s landholding on the appointed day.
The Court considered that the heirs should have an opportunity to raise other contentions and produce evidence in support of them.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the administrative orders and remanded the matter for determination of surplus land on the appointed-day basis after considering the heirs’ other contentions and supporting evidence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered the ends of justice to require an opportunity for the heirs to raise other contentions and produce evidence when the surplus land was redetermined. No earlier case or specific statutory provision was relied on for this remand direction.

predicates.appeal_in_land_ceiling_proceeding: The matter is an appeal arising from a proceeding to determine surplus agricultural land.
predicates.surplus_extent_requires_redetermination: The extent of surplus land remains to be determined after applying the governing reference-day basis.
predicates.affected_heirs_have_other_contentions_or: The affected heirs may raise contentions other than their rejected claim to separate ceiling treatment and may offer evidence supporting those contentions.
predicates.matter_is_remanded_for_redetermination_a: The matter is returned for the surplus extent to be determined after the affected heirs’ other contentions and evidence are considered.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a land-ceiling proceeding requires the surplus extent to be redetermined and affected heirs have other contentions or supporting evidence to present, the matter is remanded for redetermination after considering them.
